# Helping Your Midwife Find You

*(Written by the Riverside community midwife team, because we are the ones who get lost)*

Hiya! Welcome to Riverside Community Midwives. We are really pleased you are having your baby at home. This page is about one small job that really matters: getting us to your front door fast when baby is ready.

Please read it now, not at 3am. Then put the checklist on your fridge.

---

## First, the most important bit: when do we come?

**Home birth cover starts from 37 weeks.**

- **Before 37 weeks**, please go to the hospital if you think your baby is coming. We told you this at your booking visit, but we know it is easy to forget when you are busy and excited.
- **From 37 weeks**, we will come to your home when labour starts.

If you are not sure whether you are in labour, call us. We would much rather you call and it is nothing than wait and be worried.

---

## Calling us

**When labour starts, phone the Riverside birth line:**

**[Riverside birth line number]**

Please call the **birth line**, not a midwife's personal mobile. The birth line goes to whichever midwife is on call that night, so there is always someone to answer, even if your usual midwife is asleep or off.

**Emergency?** If you think something is seriously wrong, for example heavy bleeding, baby not breathing well, or you cannot wait for us, **call 999 first**, then call the birth line. Do not wait for us if it is an emergency.

When you call, have ready:
- Your full name and date of birth
- Your address, including your postcode
- How far apart your contractions are, and how long they last
- Whether your waters have broken, and what colour the fluid was
- Any worries you have

---

## Finding your house

This is where we need your help most. Honestly, we have all been lost at some point. Here are some things that have happened to us, so you can see why we are asking!

- One of us once drove round a block of flats in Everton for twenty minutes. Flat 14 was not near flat 13. It was in a different building. In the end, the dad was waving a tea towel out of the window at us.
- One house had only a name, "Rosemary Cottage", in a street full of terraces. The sat nav took us to a chip shop.
- One family put **balloons on the gate**, like it was a party. Best idea ever. We found it straight away.
- One of us once walked into the wrong house because the door was open. A lovely old man gave us a Jammie Dodger anyway.

So here is what helps us most:

**1. Send us a location.**
If you have a **what3words** address, send it to the birth line. Or send a **location pin on WhatsApp** to the birth line phone when you call. This is the fastest way for us to get exactly to your door.

**2. Turn on your porch light at night.**
Please, please! Dark streets in winter all look the same. A light on at your door is the easiest thing in the world to see.

**3. Make your house number clear.**
If your house has a name but no number, write the number on the gate or the bin, or put a sign in the window. Balloons are optional, but they are very welcome.

**4. Tell us if you live in a flat.**
Tell us the block name, the floor, and the flat number. Leave a light or a sign by the buzzer if you can. Please go down and open the door for us if you can.

**5. Let us know if a dog will greet us.**
See the section below!

---

## Parking

Two midwives usually come for the birth, often in **separate cars**. If you can, please keep **two parking spaces** free near your home.

Liverpool has **permit zones**, including around Anfield and Kensington. You can either:
- Apply for a **visitor permit** from the council before your due date, **or**
- Leave a **visitor permit ready on the dashboard** of each car, if we are parked in a zone.

Please check the council website for how to get a visitor permit. We have all had parking tickets before, and we really do not want to get one while your baby is being born!

---

## Carrying things

We carry a lot. We bring gas and air cylinders, the big bag with all our equipment, and sometimes birthing pool equipment too. Our arms get very tired, and we often need to carry things up stairs and through narrow hallways.

**Please help us by:**
- Clearing a route from the front door to the room where the birth will happen
- Keeping the stairs and hallway clear
- Keeping the path to the door clear too

---

## Your home, getting ready

Please clear the stairs and hallway before labour starts. This helps us move quickly and keeps everyone safe. Please remove:

- **Shoes** from the hallway and stairs
- **Washing baskets** (and washing!)
- **Lego, toys, and anything else** a midwife might trip over while holding a cylinder

You do not need to tidy the whole house. Just clear the path.

---

## Pets

We love dogs. We really do. Our midwife Pippin-loving colleague can tell you about the time a Staffie jumped on her every single visit and she nearly dropped the Entonox.

But please **put pets in another room** when we arrive and during the birth. A very friendly dog is still a lot of noise and movement when you are pushing, and it can make things harder for everyone.

---

## What to expect from us

We will be kind, calm, and honest with you. We are here to support you and your baby, not to judge how your house looks or how you are feeling. You do not have to be perfect for us.

In the Philippines, we say that the midwife is like family. That is how we want you to feel about us. We are not coming as strangers. We are coming as your friends, to help you through one of the biggest days of your life.

---

## Fridge checklist

*Print this and stick it on the fridge. Tick each box when it is done.*

**Before 37 weeks**
- ☐ I know to go to the hospital if labour starts before 37 weeks
- ☐ I have the birth line number saved in my phone

**From 37 weeks**
- ☐ The birth line number is on the fridge and in my phone
- ☐ I know to call the birth line, not a personal mobile
- ☐ I know to call 999 first in an emergency

**Finding us**
- ☐ I have a what3words address, or I can send a WhatsApp location pin
- ☐ My house number is clear from the road
- ☐ My porch light works and is on at night
- ☐ If I live in a flat, I know how to let the midwives in

**Parking**
- ☐ I have two parking spaces free, or I have arranged for them
- ☐ I have a visitor permit, or I know how to get one

**Getting the house ready**
- ☐ Stairs and hallway are clear
- ☐ Shoes are moved out of the way
- ☐ Washing baskets and toys are moved out of the way
- ☐ Pets are ready to go into another room

**Calling us**
- ☐ I have my name, date of birth, and address ready
- ☐ I know how far apart my contractions are, and when they started

---

*Thank you for reading! We are looking forward to meeting you, and we promise to find your house. Probably on the first try.*
